source.title: Safety Alignment via Constrained Knowledge Unlearning
source.authors: Zesheng Shi; Yucheng Zhou; Jing Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some results are only shown in figures, without numeric values in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies its own unlearning method and evaluates post-unlearning behavior under jailbreak attacks, conceptually testing whether attacks still elicit harmful behavior. It does not reproduce the original unlearning methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports jailbreak attack success rates after CKU unlearning, plus qualitative or tabular GCG results for CKU settings. It does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance, recovery through post-unlearning fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. The attack prompts in the appendix are example prompts, not instructions to an AI reviewer.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes CKU, a gradient-ascent safety-unlearning method, and reports only its own method's jailbreak ASR against the base model and other defenses. ASR counts responses that lack refusal keywords. That is a refusal measure, not a measure of targeted knowledge or of recovering unlearned knowledge. No forget-set accuracy is reported, and there is no ASR for the unlearned model without attack, so recovery cannot be computed. No relearning, ablation or quantization attack is run. The study relies on unlearning as a tool and benchmarks its defense, so it falls under T4, not T1, T2, T3 or T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CKU significantly improves jailbreak resistance with minimal utility loss and gives a better safety-utility trade-off than existing defenses. They acknowledge that some harmful content persists, so ASR does not reach 0%.
record.recipe_differences: CKU uses gradient-ascent unlearning with gradients pruned for selected knowledge-related MLP neurons; it is not a reproduction of the cited unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to neuron locking rate, unlearning-layer selection, neuron-selection method, regularization parameter λ, and the presence or absence of a system prompt. It identifies neuron locking rate 0.8 and MLP layers 8 to 12 as favorable settings; generation-exploitation ASR is much higher without a system prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: CKU-unlearned Llama2-7B-Chat and Llama3-8B-Instruct have lower refusal-keyword jailbreak ASR than the base models and most baseline defenses. Under decoding-exploitation attack without a system prompt, ASR stays high (71% and 69%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety unlearning by gradient ascent reduces, but does not eliminate, non-refusal under jailbreaks, as measured by refusal-string matching.

record.problems: The jailbreak ASR metric uses string matching for refusal keywords rather than direct measurement of recovered knowledge. ASR uncertainty is not reported. No model that never learned the harmful knowledge is used as a comparison. The reported ASR values remain nonzero in most conditions, and the no-system-prompt generation-exploitation results are high.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Table 2 utility-benchmark values are not recorded as separate findings because they do not measure the attack or recovery behavior in the claim.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy is reported, near-chance or otherwise. Only refusal-keyword ASR and general utility are measured.
No activation ablation and no access-versus-deletion analysis.
Jailbreaks are run, but the only measure is refusal string matching against the base model. Recovery of unlearned knowledge is not measured, and there is no unattacked unlearned baseline.
CKU's robustness is shown only as lower refusal-keyword ASR than other defenses. Knowledge recovery under any attack is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 says qualitatively that unlearned models may give 'ignorance-based refusal' while still including harmful advice. This is relevant in spirit, but it is not quantified. Table 4 adds Qwen2.5-7B utility results only. The record's labels treated a base-model comparison as recovery, which it is not.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy or show that it reaches near chance. General utility is measured, but the complete version's combination of near-chance target accuracy and attack recovery is not tested.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation is performed, and the paper does not test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No quantization of unlearned weights is tested.
Tests jailbreak attacks, but not rephrasing alone, other languages, or in-context information as recovery methods.
Tests CKU against jailbreak attacks, not recovery by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting-only methods outside the tested jailbreak attacks.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Generation exploitation attack without a system prompt
reader_labels.reason: CKU models still have ASR values of 71.00% and 69.00%, indicating substantial harmful-response success in this tested jailbreak setting (r7, r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: AIM, GCG, AutoDAN, and generation exploitation with a system prompt
reader_labels.reason: Attack success remains measurable but is substantially below the corresponding base-model values in these conditions; the results do not show recovery to the base-model rate (r1-r6, r8-r14, r16-r21).
